messages: maya: dropping a quick mock of the compact playground streaming controls — screenshot attached (see design-bot upload). Stop | Regenerate next to token badge in the top-right. question: is the token counter being visible + live updates okay for a11y? also worried about the label 'Stop' — can mean different things. any quick takes? design-bot: uploaded image playground-controls-v3.png :camera_with_flash: sam: looks nice. couple of engineering notes: - streaming write uses incremental DOM patches right now, the token badge re-renders every 300ms which causes slight layout jitter. - if we keep the token badge in the top-right we should debounce updates and avoid changing its width. - accessibility: make sure the stop/regenerate controls are native buttons with role=button and keyboard focus. emily: copy thoughts: - "Stop" feels abrupt. alternatives: "Interrupt" / "Pause" / "Cancel generation". - short tooltip for screen readers: provide aria-label like `Interrupt generation` and a visually-hidden hint that regeneration will preserve last output unless user wants it cleared. - for the token counter microcopy: prefer concise "Tokens used: 1,234" rather than just a number. liam: a11y nits and suggestions: - streaming content should be in an `aria-live="polite"` region so screen readers hear the incremental output but not flood users. - the token counter should not be constantly announced. instead maintain a visually-hidden `aria-live` region that updates less frequently (on milestone or on demand). - ensure token badge contrast >= 4.5:1 for text/icons; if it's small text, consider 7:1. - keyboard: pressing Enter on the Stop/Interrupt button should stop generation and move focus to the regenerated result container. maya: good. on the regenerate flow — do we clear the message while regenerating or keep previous + show a spinner overlay? UX preference? sam: implementation-wise it's simpler to keep last output and overlay a subtle spinner/stripe labelled "Regenerating". that avoids losing context if the new output is worse. will need CSS z-index care for token badge. emily: microcopy decision proposal: - primary action: "Interrupt" (short, action-first) - secondary: "Regenerate" - tooltip for token badge: "Tokens used in this conversation" - sr-only live text for tokens: "Tokens used: {n}" updated on pause/completion liam: +1. also add an announcement on completion like "Generation complete" with a polite live region. for very long responses we should provide a way to opt-in for continuous announcements (settings) to avoid noise. maya: quick implementation checklist then: - debounce token updates to 1s and render visually but only update sr-only live region on completion or every 50 tokens. (sam to implement) - switch label to "Interrupt" for primary (emily to write strings and tooltips) - add aria-live polite for streaming and completion announcements (liam to draft a11y QA) - preserve last output during regenerates and overlay a spinner (sam to prototype) sam: will push a small PR with the aria-live snippet and debounced token counter. snippet for review: ```html 1,234 Tokens used: 1234 ``` emily: love it. also can we add a short CTA copy under the badge for new users: "Tokens shown for transparency" — tiny text. liam: that CTA is fine visually but don't include it for screen readers (sr-only will do). also I'll add a short checklist: focus order, keyboard labels, live region tests, color contrast, color-only states. maya: ok final quick decision here in thread: label = "Interrupt"; token counter visible (debounced) + sr-only live updates on completion; preserve output during regenerate. i'll update the mock and post new image. :thumbsup: design-bot: uploaded image playground-controls-v3a.png :camera_with_flash: sam: thanks — I'll get the PR up today and tag you all for review. emily: I'll push the copy strings to i18n keys and add tooltip text. liam: I'll draft the a11y test cases and drop them into the QA doc. maya: awesome, thanks team. closing this thread for design review iteration — will reopen if any regressions pop up.
